status: Baseline fixtures only; no dependency or production change. Replacement blocked on a public behavior decision under #88.
baseline_tests: Three native fixtures: dot entries and bulk/cursor order, first-NUL truncation, immediate path errors, rename isolation and thread transfer.
current_path: osd/file/native_unix/directory_cursor.rs owns DIR, calls readdir for every next_name, copies each name once and closes the stream once. A null read returns None but does not prevent a later read.

candidates.name: std::fs::ReadDir
candidates.assessment: Not a direct replacement. Rust 1.99.0 library/std/src/sys/fs/unix.rs ReadDir::next skips '.' and '..', which the pinned fixture observes in native order, and sets end_of_stream on the first null readdir, so it fuses at end of stream and after an error. The current cursor calls readdir again on every next_name.

candidates.name: rustix 1.1.5 Dir
candidates.assessment: The default Linux backend retries interrupted reads. Both backends retain an any_errors flag that prevents subsequent reads after an error. The libc backend can avoid the Linux retry change via use-libc, but still fuses after errors. Entries own a CString; copying into the existing Vec return type adds a name allocation relative to the current path. Costs are not measured yet.
candidates.recovery_limit: seek clears the error flag, but preserving position requires a valid cookie. The libc DirEntry::offset API is not available on macOS; no portable retry-preserving adapter has been demonstrated.
candidates.cleanup: With use-libc (the feature Martensite already enables), Dir::new takes an OwnedFd and closes the raw descriptor itself when fdopendir fails, so failure cleanup needs no first-party shim. Opening with rustix::fs::open(RDONLY|DIRECTORY|CLOEXEC|NONBLOCK) matches the glibc and Apple opendir flags; ENOENT and ENOTDIR stay the same.
candidates.conflict: Dir::read sets any_errors after a null readdir with non-zero errno and returns None on every later read until rewind or seek. End of stream does not set the flag, so EOF re-reads match. The only divergence is the next_name call after a read error: the current cursor retries readdir, rustix returns None. The public directory iterator drops the cursor at the first None, so it cannot observe the difference; a direct caller of the public PosixFileCalls::open_directory and DirectoryEntries::next_name can.
candidates.cost: DirEntry owns a CString and exposes only file_name(&CStr), so the existing Vec<u8> return adds one allocation and copy per entry. Not measured.

candidates.name: rustix 1.1.5 RawDir
candidates.assessment: Borrows a caller-owned mutable buffer, exposes borrowed names, and calls getdents_uninit without a retry loop in RawDir::next. Reconstructing it for each next_name would discard unread buffered entries. A safe owned-cursor design and supported-target coverage remain unproven; this is not a reason to hide a self-reference cast in a helper.

candidates.name: nix 0.31.3 Dir/OwningIter
candidates.assessment: OwningIter does not fuse read errors, but Dir::from_fd leaks the consumed descriptor on fdopendir failure. The isolated safe probe reproduced ENOTDIR with the descriptor still open twice under Rust 1.99.0. Tracked as Bug #126; nix was not added to Martensite. Entry owns a CString, so allocation costs also need measurement.
candidates.older_version_check: The local 0.29.0 source closes on constructor failure but uses the older readdir_r representation; upstream v0.30.1 has the consumed-descriptor leak. No older version was adopted.

next_requirements: Maintainer decision on the #88 conflict above
If accepted: an injected read-failure fixture that pins the chosen post-error behavior
Measure per-entry allocations, elapsed time and peak memory before adoption
Run native fixtures on all affected supported targets
scope_limit: No impossibility or permanent system exception is established. The existing unsafe cursor remains temporary migration work.
merge_base: origin/main merged at 38b684d before the native rehearsal

options: Accept fuse-after-read-error for DirectoryEntries::next_name (document it on the trait) and adopt rustix Dir under forbid(unsafe_code).
Keep retry-after-error as a contract; then no current dependency satisfies it and the unsafe cursor stays until a safe API without error fusing is available.
decision_request.not_options: nix Dir until #126 is fixed in a release; std::fs::ReadDir because it drops dot entries and fuses at end of stream.

native_rehearsal.result: success on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (Unix fixtures are compiled out on Windows)
native_rehearsal.local_gate: cargo xtask pr passed on Linux x86_64 with Rust 1.99.0
